When there is an agreed period that sees the gas pipeline not being utilized the materials, modules and equipment can be lifted by crane across and into the site. Subject to the adjacent site owner's standard procedures or requirements, crossing this pipeline should be agreed and developed during an early project stage. Risk assessments for the crane- lifts will most likely indicate that ‘dropped object protection’ (DOP) over the pipeline will be necessary. Marine Off-Loading to Site Transfers (Option 2) Options for DOP could be developed with just a temporary type of steelwork reinforced arch structure as a protection barrier specifically for the crane works, or a more robust purpose-built heavy-duty bridge crossover. By forming elevated civil ground works and building a concrete barrier wall on either side of the pipeline a Bailey type bridge can be laid out and positioned across. With this bridge in place, in addition to providing for more substantial pipeline protection at all times, it allows for the capacity of the safe working load crossings to be increased, with loaded SPMT’s transferring directly onto site. Marine Off-Loading by Crane or SPMT Material load transfers could remain flexible but would depend on what lift-plan options become acceptable. One option would involve heavy crane lifts from the cargo barge directly into site area, then transferred for positioning to foundations by mobile cranes. Another would involve lifting material already preloaded on SMPT’s off the cargo barge, transferring it across onto the embankment area, over a Bailey bridge directly adjacent to the foundations (single transfer operation), and then finally positioned by local mobile cranes. Marine Off-Loading Summary The crossover bridge facility could remain and be utilized for the site’s next construction phase of ‘future’ development, as well as for any possible maintenance tasks. However, the pontoon access could be removed and brought back in as and when further construction works were required. 4.10.4 DELIVERY AND INSTALLATION OF EQUIPMENT AND FACILITIES Materials, fabricated modules and packaged equipment will be shipped by barge (where too large to be trucked on public roads) or by truck to the site in a logical sequence to support fabrication. As large, heavy items such as the storage tanks and large pre-assembled units (PAUs) are delivered by barge they can be transferred directly onto site via SPMTs crossing the pipeline as necessary.
